arbeitnow-nous-operations-automation-ass.title: Operations & Automation Associate
arbeitnow-nous-operations-automation-ass.description: About Nous Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute. We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money. We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked. Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent. And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people". The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build. The role What Nous does for members can feel simple: helping them understand their bills, save money, and avoid admin. Delivering that reliably at scale is much harder. You’ll join the Operations team at the heart of the business, working on the difficult real-world problems that sit between our members, our product, external suppliers and the systems that make Nous work. This is not a traditional customer operations role. You’ll spend time close to our members, understanding their questions, investigating things that have gone wrong and learning in detail how our service works. We think that matters: the best systems are usually built by people who have seen the underlying problems first-hand. But we don’t want you simply to get faster at doing manual work. We want you to spot the pattern, understand why the problem exists, and help build a better way of doing it. That might mean redesigning a process, building an automation, using AI to remove repetitive work, querying data to understand what is happening, improving an internal tool, or working with Product and Engineering on a more fundamental fix. You don't need to arrive knowing all of the tools we use. We care much more about how quickly you learn them. We’re looking for someone early in their career who is unusually curious, quick to learn and good at figuring things out. You might already have built automations or small products yourself. You might instead have worked in operations, consulting, product, analytics or another demanding environment and found yourself constantly looking for better ways to do things. Either way, we want someone who gets excited by a problem they don't immediately know how to solve. You’ll have a lot of support from experienced operators, engineers and product people, but also be given a lot of responsibility unusually early in your career. The aim is for you to quickly become someone who can take an undefined operational problem, understand it properly and build a robust solution. It’s a rare chance to learn how a fast-growing technology company actually works from the inside while building the systems that allow it to scale. About you You’re smart, curious, ambitious and unusually high-agency. You don't need a long list of technical tools on your CV. We care much more about how you think, how quickly you learn and what you do when you encounter something you don't understand. You’ll probably thrive here if you: Have roughly 1–3 years of experience in a demanding environment such as a startup, operations, consulting, product, analytics or similar Learn unusually quickly and enjoy tackling problems you haven't seen before Are technically curious and actively experiment with AI and new tools to make yourself more effective Have evidence that you like building things, whether that's automations, side projects, spreadsheets, scripts, internal tools, processes or something completely different Are comfortable getting into the detail and tracing a problem until you understand what is really happening Can take something messy and ambiguous and impose structure on it Are naturally empathetic and enjoy understanding what a customer actually needs Communicate clearly and directly Are comfortable working directly with customers and frontline problems, and see that as a source of insight Take ownership rather than waiting to be told exactly what to do This role is ideal for someone early in their career who wants a steep learning curve, real responsibility and the chance to work as part of a team solving difficult problems. arbeitnow-fractile-chief-information-sec.description: About Fractile Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts. The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems. Fractile is building the next generation of AI computing technology, developing innovative hardware and software solutions designed to transform the performance and efficiency of AI workloads. We're bringing together exceptional talent across semiconductor engineering, software, and AI to solve some of the most ambitious challenges in computing. You will be responsible for developing and executing a comprehensive technology and security strategy, ensuring Fractile's systems, infrastructure, intellectual property, and business operations are secure, reliable, and scalable. This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role, combining cybersecurity expertise with ownership of IT operations, infrastructure, and service delivery. arbeitnow-faculty-machine-learning-engin.description: Why Faculty? We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here . We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence. Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology. AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen. About the team Our National Security and AI Safety business unit is dedicated to advancing the responsible development and deployment of AI in support of national security and global stability. From strengthening mission-critical capabilities across national security and intelligence, to working with frontier labs to provide robust AI safety red teaming and evaluation, we work at the frontier of high-stakes, high-impact missions. We understand that powerful AI systems bring both transformative opportunities and complex risks and we are proud to partner with Government and the biggest tech organisations in the world to ensure AI is not just transformative but is also secure, trustworthy and safe for all. About the role Join us as a Machine Learning Engineer to deliver bespoke, impactful AI solutions for our diverse clients. You will bridge the gap between AI research and real-world impact by building scalable, production-grade machine learning systems. Partnering with clients and cross-functional teams, you will champion technical feasibility, ensure seamless delivery, and collaborate with Frontier Labs to reinforce our leadership in practical, high-stakes AI safety. What you'll be doing: Building and deploying production-grade ML software, tools, and infrastructure. Creating reusable, scalable solutions that accelerate the delivery of ML systems and capability testing of Frontier AI models. Collaborating with engineers, data scientists, and commercial leads to solve critical client challenges. Leading technical scoping and architectural decisions to ensure project feasibility and impact. Defining and implementing Faculty’s standards for deploying machine learning at scale. Acting as a technical advisor to customers and partners, translating complex ML concepts for stakeholders. Who we're looking for: You are comfortable building LLM applications, and are familiar with multi-agent harness tooling and AI Safety evaluation procedures. You possess strong Python skills and solid experience in software engineering best practices. You bring hands-on experience with cloud platforms and infrastructure (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP), including architecture and security. You've worked with container and orchestration tools such at Docker & Kubernetes to build and manage applications at scale You are comfortable with core ML concepts, including probability, statistics, and common learning techniques. You understand the full machine learning lifecycle and have experience operationalising models built with frameworks like Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, or PyTorch. You're an excellent communicator, able to guide technical teams and confidently advise non-technical stakeholders. You thrive in a fast-paced environment, and enjoy the autonomy to own scope, solve and delivery solutions Our Interview Process Talent Team Screen (30 minutes) Pair Programming Interview (90 minutes) System Design Interview (90 minutes) Commercial Interview (60 minutes) #LI-PRIO Our Recruitment Ethos We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations. If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI. arbeitnow-anthropic-staff-software-secur.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

The Security Engineering team's mission is to safeguard our AI systems and maintain the trust of our users and society at large. Whether we're developing critical security infrastructure, building secure development practices, or partnering with our research and product teams, we are committed to operating as a world-class security organization and keeping the safety and trust of our users at the forefront of everything we do.

Responsibilities:

  • Build security for large-scale AI clusters across multiple clouds and bare-metal data centers, including IAM, network segmentation and encryption controls
  • Design and implement network security controls: default-deny ingress and egress, segmentation between research, training and production environments, private connectivity across clouds and data centers, cloud firewall policy and mTLS with service identity
  • Ship these controls as secure defaults using infrastructure as code and GitOps workflows, so new clusters, VPCs and data center links inherit the right boundaries
  • Build visibility into network traffic and boundary drift, with detection for exfiltration paths and automated remediation where it is safe to do so
  • Design secure-by-design development workflows and CI/CD pipelines across our services, with expertise in Kubernetes security, container orchestration and identity management
  • Threat model and assess risk for complex multi cloud and networked environments, and join infrastructure networking, cluster and data center teams at design time so topology, routing and firewall decisions carry our security requirements from day one
  • Mentor engineers and contribute to hiring and growth of the Security team

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Have 8-15+ years of software engineering experience implementing and maintaining critical systems at scale
  • Strong software engineering skills in Python or at least one systems language (Go, Rust, C/C++)
  • Experience implementing and operating critical systems at scale using DevOps and cloud automation practices such as infrastructure as code
  • Hands-on network security engineering in cloud or on-prem environments, for example VPC design, cloud firewall policy, egress control, private service connectivity or network segmentation
  • Working knowledge of Kubernetes security and networking, including network policy, service identity and container hardening
  • Experience with threat modeling and risk assessment for networked and multi cloud systems
  • Track record of driving engineering excellence through high standards, constructive code reviews and mentorship
  • Clear communicator who can translate technical concepts across organizational levels and bring clarity and ownership to ambiguous technical problems
  • Low ego, high empathy engineer who attracts talent and supports diverse, inclusive teams
  • Experience supporting fast-paced startup engineering teams

Strong candidates may also have experience with:

  • Secured Kubernetes networking at scale (CNI, network policy, service mesh or mTLS rollouts) or worked in high-assurance environments where controls had to be evidenced, not just deployed
  • Worked on interconnects and private connectivity between cloud providers and physical data centers, including management-plane and out-of-band network security
  • Built network traffic visibility or exfiltration detection systems
  • Exposure to large-scale distributed training and what it demands of a network
  • Led cross-functional security initiatives and navigated complex organizational dynamics
  • Managing infrastructure through automated configuration and policy enforcement
  • Hardening containerized applications and enforcing security policies

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Senior Product Engineer 

Engineering

 

 Prolific

Prolific is not just another player in the AI space – we are the architects of the human data infrastructure that's reshaping the landscape of AI development. In a world where foundational AI technologies are increasingly commoditized, it's the quality and diversity of human-generated data that truly differentiates products and models.

 

The role

We’re looking for Senior Product Engineers with a ‘product builder’ mind-set to join our team and take a pivotal role in the development and guidance of our product. As a ‘t-shaped’ engineer, you will bring a broad practical knowledge across various areas of software development, complementing and supporting our growing team whilst likely having a deeper specialism in front or backend. This is an exciting opportunity to leverage your existing skills, experience, and knowledge to significantly influence the trajectory of our product as we aim to revolutionize research.

 

What you’ll bring to the role

  • Deep understanding of modern web applications
  • Experience building Typescript/Javascript applications and using NoSQL databases
  • Experience using Python
  • Knowledge of Event-Driven Architecture
  • Experience using AWS (Serverless) and/or GCP
  • Understand the importance of driving quality into code through test automation
  • Have supported applications in production, with demonstrable experience of good observability practices within a full stack environment. (e.g. Rum, Tracing)
  • Have worked in a collaborative environment with strong engineering practices and know what good engineering looks like
  • Care about the product life cycle and are customer value focused
  • Understand the value of continuous, iterative improvement using data to drive decisions and a culture of feedback
  • Passionate about software development with an appetite for learning and self-improvement

 

What you’ll be doing in the role 

  • As a member of a cross-functional, stream-aligned team, you will work collaboratively with the teams’ engineering manager, product manager, designer, and up to 4-5 other engineers, including a tech lead
  • Using agile software development practices and a product mindset, you will work as a team to plan, build and support software that our customers love
  • You will be highly self-motivated and energetic and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment with a bias for action
  • Collaborating with teams outside of product engineering, working closely with customers and understanding their needs
  • Be happy working in all the major cloud providers: AWS, GCP & Azure
  • With a You Build It, You Run It mindset, you will have intimate knowledge of our products from code commit through to production operation
  • Supporting production systems with monitoring tools such as Datadog
  • Strive for stable systems observability
  • You will champion our principles, fuel a growth mindset by getting involved in communities and help improve our engineering culture
  • Pushing the boundaries, questioning the status quo, ensuring what we are doing and what we are building has high value and impact for our users

 

Key Technologies 

  • Cloud Platforms: Google Cloud Platform and AWS
  • Programming Languages: Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript
  • Frameworks: Vue.js, Django Rest Framework, Container-based and Serverless architectures
  • Databases: MongoDB and DynamoDB
  • DevOps and Monitoring: CircleCI, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, Celery, EventBridge and DataDog

 

Why Prolific is a great place to work

We've built a unique platform that connects researchers and companies with a global pool of participants, enabling the collection of high-quality, ethically sourced human behavioral data and feedback. This data

arbeitnow-ocadogroup-senior-software-eng.title: Senior Software Engineer - Data & ML
arbeitnow-ocadogroup-senior-software-eng.description:
Senior Software Engineer – Data & ML | Autoplanner | Hybrid Working | London

Introduction: 

We are Ocado Group, and we're bringing world-class automation to online grocery. Our Ocado Smart Platform (OSP) combines cutting-edge robotics, AI, and IoT within our advanced CFCs (Customer Fulfilment Centres). We've mastered the single pick, transforming online delivery for our global partners. Join us and be part of a team pushing the boundaries of retail technology. 

About the Role:

As a Senior Software Engineer in the Autoplanner team, you will own the software engineering that brings our data science and machine learning products into live production. Autoplanner builds AI-powered systems that unify planning across global warehouses and last-mile assets, delivering globally optimized plans that maximize profit and minimize lateness. You will act as the engineering partner to our data scientists, ensuring our systems remain robust, highly scalable, and efficient as we roll out to more international retail partners. Our services are mostly Python, but we use Java where a service integrates closely with the Ocado Smart Platform, to take advantage of its shared tooling.

In this role, you will write typed, well-tested Python and oversee cloud-based data applications from end to end. You will contribute to core architectural decisions, improve CI/CD pipelines, and raise engineering standards across the team through pairing, code reviews, and shared tooling. Additionally, you will harness AI coding tools in production while maintaining a strong emphasis on engineering discipline, system performance, and high-quality software craft.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and maintain data- and ML-driven, cloud-based applications.
  • Build and maintain robust APIs and data contracts for data science teams and broader Ocado systems.
  • Manage cloud deployments and continuously improve CI/CD pipelines across diverse AWS environments.
  • Package, version, serve, and monitor machine learning models in live production environments.
  • Drive architecture decisions across repository, application, and system levels, documenting them as Architecture Decision Records (ADRs).
  • Partner directly with data scientists to transition advanced algorithms and models into scalable production systems.
  • Collaborate with software engineers across Ocado Technology to integrate applications within the Ocado Smart Platform (OSP).
  • Elevate engineering practices across the team through pairing, code reviews, shared tooling, and responsible AI agent integration.
  • Share in on-call and production support responsibilities for critical live operational services.

What We’re Looking For:

  • Proven experience as a Senior Software Engineer owning end-to-end production Python services.
  • Extensive background building data-intensive cloud applications, preferably asynchronous, event-driven, or queue-based architectures.
  • Strong practical knowledge of AWS and/or GCP identity, networking, and messaging services.
  • Solid software design capabilities, including defining system boundaries and crafting high-level architectures.
  • Rigorous testing and delivery discipline, encompassing integration testing and modern CI/CD practices.
  • Hands-on MLOps experience, specifically in packaging, serving, and monitoring ML models in production.
  • Demonstrated track record of collaborating effectively with data scientists and cross-functional engineering teams.
  • Practical experience using AI coding agents on production codebases, with a sharp judgment on validating and verifying AI-generated output.

Benefits:

We believe in supporting our people with meaningful, flexible benefits that prioritise well-being and work-life balance. Here’s a snapshot of what you can expect:

  • Time to recharge: 25 days annual leave (rising to 27 after 5 years), plus the option to buy more – and 30 days a year to work from anywhere in the world.
  • Health & wellbeing: Private Medical Insurance from your first month, wellbeing support through specialist apps and EAP, plus Income Protection and Life Assurance.
  • Family-first policies: 22 weeks paid maternity/primary carer leave and 6 weeks paid paternity leave.
  • Financial support: Pension with employer matching up to 7%, share schemes (Sharesave & BAYE), and interest-free loans for train tickets.
  • Commuter perks: Cycle to Work Scheme and free shuttle buses to/from Hatfield and Welwyn Garden City stations.
  • Exclusive discounts: 15% off at Ocado.com with free delivery (starting in your first month).

Be bold, be unique, be brilliant, be you. We are looking for individuality and we value diversity. We are an equal opportunities employer and we are committed to treating all applicants and employees fairly and equally. We are committed to making reasonable adjustments to provide a positive, barrier-free recruitment process and supportive work environment. If you have any support or access requirements, we encourage you to advise us at the time of application.

Our mission-critical models drive key operational decisions for global partners, including demand forecasting, drive-time predictions, and supplier reliability. In this role, you will own the full data science lifecycle, from researching state-of-the-art deep learning techniques to deploying, scaling, and supporting production-ready models.

Working closely with cross-functional software engineering, data engineering, and product teams, you will tackle high-impact problems where algorithm performance directly affects operational efficiency and partner revenue. arbeitnow-lua-sales-development-represen.title: Sales Development Representative, UK & Europe
arbeitnow-lua-sales-development-represen.description: Lua is the Agent OS. We build digital employees: agents that do a real job end to end. They read a company's own systems, make the decision, take the action, and get a little better every time they run. Not chatbots that answer questions, but digital workers that do the work, on the company's own data and workflows, and everything they build stays owned by the business. Teams write their logic on Lua (agents, skills, tools, jobs, webhooks, guardrails) and we run the hard parts underneath: infrastructure, multi-provider model orchestration, data, channels (WhatsApp, Slack, email, Instagram, Messenger, a voice-capable website widget, HTTP API) and monitoring. About us Our customers are the companies that run their markets: the operator of one of the world's most-visited heritage sites, a major travel and hospitality group, the largest supermarket chain in its country, a listed conglomerate spanning healthcare and consumer goods, large regional banks, a social-commerce company and a microinsurer covering over a million people, across Africa, the Middle East and South Asia. Together they employ 64,000+ people and turn over $5bn+ a year, and they all want the same thing: to be AI-native on the systems they already run, with nothing to rip out. We are a lean team of 30, backed by Y Combinator, and we've raised $5.8M. We have deployed 10,000+ agents across 20 markets. Having scaled from emerging markets, we are now moving into the UK and Europe. This is our founding commercial hire in the region and, based on performance, will quickly convert into an AE Europe role. The role As Lua's first SDR in Europe, you sit at the top of the UK and EU revenue funnel and report to Hugo de Stacpoole, VP of Sales. You will prospect personally into priority mid-market and enterprise accounts using LinkedIn, phone, email, events and warm introductions. You will also direct an AI-native outbound stack that handles research, sequencing and first-touch personalisation, and step in when a human conversation will do more than another automated touch. There is no playbook yet. You will help define how Lua sources, qualifies and hands opportunities to Account Executives in the region, including the qualification criteria. You are judged on qualified pipeline and revenue contribution, not activity alone. What you'll do Run outbound end to end. Identify target accounts and decision-makers across the UK and Europe and book qualified meetings for the sales team. Maintain a prioritised target account list with AEs and leadership, and tune it using results. Direct and refine our AI SDR tooling. Set up, monitor and improve automated sequences and enrichment workflows. Qualify with discipline. Run early discovery and pass only opportunities that meet agreed criteria. Hand over cleanly to sales and help define the handoff standard. Track funnel quality from outreach to meeting to qualified opportunity to revenue, and act on the gaps. Keep the CRM accurate so the team has a reliable view of the pipeline. Sharpen the pitch by feeding back what prospects actually say. Track the market, including competitors, buyer trends and regulation such as the EU AI Act. Support partners and events that turn into new pipeline. What we're looking for You have been the first SDR somewhere and built the outbound motion from nothing. Two or more years of B2B prospecting, ideally selling SaaS, AI or other technology to mid-market or enterprise buyers. You can talk credibly about AI and AI use cases across multiple industries. You know the UK market well. A European network or a second European language is a plus. You can explain to a senior executive in a few sentences why Lua is worth their time. You use AI outreach, enrichment and automation tools well, and you spot weak output quickly. You manage your own pipeline and keep the CRM accurate without being reminded. Experience at AI-native startups, B2B SaaS teams or expert networks is a strong fit. Familiarity with Apollo, Clay and the major LLMs is a plus. How success is measured Meetings booked and held, qualified opportunities created, pipeline generated (direct and partner-sourced), stage conversion, handoff acceptance and speed, CRM data quality, and closed-won revenue from SDR-sourced opportunities. What we offer $38k base plus commission Equity incentive plan 25 days holiday per year, pro rata London, hybrid, with minimal office time required A direct path into a closing AE role, or into onboarding the next SDRs as the team grows If you want to build Lua's European sales motion from the first account, let's talk. arbeitnow-accurx-information-security-ri.title: Information Security & Risk Officer
arbeitnow-accurx-information-security-ri.description: 💬 Accurx is solving healthcare productivity for the NHS. For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that make simple tasks feel impossible. At Accurx, we’re changing that by building a single, system-wide platform that helps every patient get gold-standard, efficient, and joined-up care. What started as a way for GPs to text a patient has now evolved into an all-in-one digital toolkit used by 98% of GP practices. Our platform now powers Total Triage to manage patient demand, and Self-Book , which lets patients schedule their own appointments in seconds. We’ve automated routine care with Patient Questionnaires for long-term conditions, while Accumail finally allows staff-to-staff communication to happen instantly across different care settings. We’re now pushing the boundaries of the consultation itself with Accurx Scribe , our AI-powered note-taker that drafts medical notes in real-time. We’re not just shipping features. We’re giving clinicians their time back and ensuring every patient journey is as smooth as it should be. The role It's a hands-on, delivery-focused role, and you'll make an impact from the start in risk management, security advisory, customer and tender responses, audit readiness and our data strategy. This isn't a security engineering role. You won't configure firewalls or run vulnerability scans. Instead, you'll understand our technical environment well enough to spot risks and gaps, then recommend best practices for Engineering, DevOps and IT to put in place. A background in compliance management alone won't be enough for this role. You'll report to our Senior Information Security Officer, who owns our GRC framework, ISO 27001 programme, CE/CE+ & DSPT compliance, and the security risk register. You'll help deliver across all of it. Challenges you’ll solve... Own risk management: run risk sessions across the business, keep the risk register current, write clear risk reports and chase treatment actions to completion Advise the business: be the security voice with Engineering, DevOps, IT and Product, and a first point of contact for security questions from every team Handle customers, tenders and suppliers: answer security questionnaires and tenders accurately, and assess suppliers before we approve them Keep us audit-ready: gather evidence all year round for Cyber Essentials Plus, DSPT and ISO 27001, and flag control gaps with practical fixes Deliver our data strategy: drive the data classification and access control programmes forward with data owners You should apply if... You have hands-on infosec and risk experience : ideally in health-tech, regulated SaaS or software development. You've run risk sessions, managed a risk register and reported on risk to senior stakeholders. You possess technical depth to hold your own: You understand authentication vs authorisation, least privilege, IAM, network segmentation and firewalls, patch and vulnerability management, endpoint protection and cloud infrastructure. You understand frameworks: ISO 27001, DSPT, NIST and Cyber Essentials Plus, and a sense of what proportionate looks like in a fast-moving product company. You work fast and independently: You manage your own workload, flag blockers early and can move between a tender, a questionnaire and an engineering conversation in the same day. You care about healthcare: and know the data we protect belongs to patients and clinicians. Nice to have: enterprise risk management experience, and having been through a CE+ audit cycle. What’s in it for you? You’ll join a high-performing team on a mission to solve healthcare productivity, building a platform used by around 300k NHS staff every week, supporting the care of over 50 million NHS patients every year. We set a high bar, move fast, and give people the ownership and support to do the best work of their careers £65,000 - £75,000 salary, plus a discretionary recognition bonus for exceptional performance and impact, nominated by managers and awarded by our leadership team Equity: £15,000 in equal share options, so you share in the value you help create Benefits to suit you: adjust your healthcare cover, your pension or life insurance, whatever stage you’re at in life Built for collaboration: We are an office-first culture and ask that you’re in our (dog-friendly) Shoreditch office for a minimum of 3 days a week Close to our users: Regular hackathons, plus dedicated time to visit GP practices and other healthcare settings to see first-hand how our products are used Time off: You’ll get 28 days of holiday (plus bank holidays) and up to 4 weeks to work from anywhere per year Support at home: We offer enhanced parental leave, fertility support and parental loss support We have our very own chefs: Free healthy breakfasts, snacks and lunches, plus a weekly sweet treat Compensation: £65K – £75K • Offers Equity • £65K – £75K • Offers Equity Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

arbeitnow-ecole-nationale-superieure-de-.company: ECOLE NATIONALE SUPERIEURE DE TECHNIQUES AVANCEES
arbeitnow-ecole-nationale-superieure-de-.description: ENSTA, établissement d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche sous tutelle du ministère des Armées, développe des activités de formation, de recherche et d’innovation dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité, des transports, de l'énergie, des activités maritimes, du numérique et de la santé. L’école, présente sur deux campus, à Paris-Saclay et à Brest, est membre de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Classée dans le Top 10 des meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France, elle a pour mission : la formation d’élèves ingénieurs civils et militaires, de cadres et docteurs pour les secteurs public et privé, la recherche et l’innovation de haut niveau en relation étroite avec l’industrie des grands secteurs de souveraineté au sein de 6 unités de formation et de recherche (UFR). Le/la titulaire du poste sera affecté au sein de l’Unité de Formation et de Recherche (UFR) Mécanique. L’UFR de Mécanique a pour mission d’assurer la formation en mécanique des élèves du cursus ingénieur d’ENSTA, des élèves de masters de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, et la formation par la recherche d’étudiants français et étrangers au niveau master et doctorat. L’Unité développe également des activités de recherche dans le domaine de la mécanique des matériaux et des structures, de la mécanique des fluides, des vibrations et de l’acoustique. Ces activités sont réalisées grâce à un important parc expérimental de haut niveau en mécanique des solides et des fluides, tant pour l’enseignement que la recherche. Sur le campus de Brest, l’UFR de Mécanique compte une cinquantaine d’enseignants chercheurs, une cinquantaine de doctorants/post-doctorants ainsi qu’une dizaine de personnels techniques (ingénieurs, techniciens). Les activités de recherche des membres de l’UFR de Mécanique du site de Brest sont menées au sein de l’Institut de Recherche Dupuy de Lôme (IRDL, CNRS UMR 6027, www.irdl.fr ). La personne recrutée travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les enseignants-chercheurs de l’ENSTA, pôle thématique de recherche « Structure Interaction Fluide (StIF) » de l’IRDL. L’ENSTA est l’un des partenaires du projet SEARENITY, retenu dans le cadre de l'appel à projets « CORIMER Navire Bas Carbone » (financement Ademe, France 2030). Le projet vise à développer un robot autonome capable d’intervenir en continu sur les coques de navires pour les nettoyer et limiter l’apparition d’algues et coquillages afin de réduire sa consommation énergétique et ses émissions de C02. L’ENSTA intervient sur 2 aspects du projet pour lequel les verrous techniques sont nombreux et pointus : le système d’attraction magnétique : définition, simulation et tests. le volet hydrodynamique du robot : modélisation, simulation numérique et essais en veine aérodynamique La présente fiche de poste concerne les aspects hydrodynamiques. Missions / Activités principales : La personne recrutée prendra en charge l’évaluation numérique des efforts subis par le robot dans différentes configurations d’opération, et proposera des pistes d’optimisation de forme, afin d’améliorer les performances. Les modèles développés seront également confrontés à des essais de validation dans la nouvelle veine aérodynamique de l’école. Elle sera amenée à produire des rapports et présentations techniques, mettre en œuvre des outils de simulation numérique et des essais, et travailler de manière collaborative avec l’ensemble des partenaires du projet SEARENITY. Les missions détaillées sont les suivantes : Etude expérimentale en soufflerie Essais de caractérisation et de validation en veine aérodynamique, afin de valider les simulations numériques pour l’estimation des efforts, en fonction de différents paramètres (influence de la vitesse de l’écoulement, influence de l’angle d’incidence). Mise en place du protocole d’essais, conception du support et impression 3D du modèle réduit de drone, calibrage des capteurs, mise en œuvre de la veine aérodynamique. 2. Etude numérique pour le fonctionnement en zone immergée Détermination numérique des efforts moyens rencontrés par le drone en condition réelle le long de la coque. Les simulations numériques seront réalisées avec un code de calcul commercial validé, constituant l’une des références à l’heure actuelle pour la simulation d’écoulements à haut Reynolds. 3. Dimensionnement des efforts d’impact en splash-zone Détermination numérique des efforts d’impact à la traversée de la surface libre, pour différentes vitesses du navire, et différents angles d’incidence du drone. Les simulations numériques seront réalisées à l’aide d’un code de calcul développé par l’ENSTA, spécifiquement dédié aux cas d’impacts. Plusieurs trajectoires de rentrée dans l’eau seront simulées, afin de cerner les efforts maximaux subis par la structure. 4. Optimisation de forme du robot Le fonctionnement nominal du drone en zone immergée, et la phase d’entrée dans l’eau conduisent à des formes géométriques optimales très différentes. Une étude bibliographique sera menée pour orienter la recherche d’une forme extérieure la plus adaptée, au sens d’un compromis sur les efforts acceptables. Cette étude bibliographique sera éventuellement complétée par des calculs de traînée et d’impact sur des géométries académiques, afin de fournir une aide à la décision pour les concepteurs du drone. arbeitnow-ecole-nationale-superieure-de-.description: ENSTA, établissement d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche sous tutelle du ministère des Armées, développe des activités de formation, de recherche et d’innovation dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité, des transports, de l'énergie, des activités maritimes, du numérique et de la santé. L’Unité développe également des activités de recherche dans le domaine de la mécanique des matériaux et des structures, de la mécanique des fluides, des vibrations et de l’acoustique. Ces activités sont réalisées grâce à un important parc expérimental de haut niveau en mécanique des solides et des fluides, tant pour l’enseignement que la recherche. Sur le campus de Brest, l’UFR de Mécanique compte une cinquantaine d’enseignants chercheurs, une cinquantaine de doctorants/post-doctorants ainsi qu’une dizaine de personnels techniques (ingénieurs, techniciens). Les activités de recherche des membres de l’UFR de Mécanique du site de Brest sont menées au sein de l’Institut de Recherche Dupuy de Lôme (IRDL, CNRS UMR 6027, www.irdl.fr ). La personne recrutée travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les enseignants-chercheurs de l’ENSTA, pôle thématique de recherche « Structure Interaction Fluide (StIF) » de l’IRDL. Le recrutement s’inscrit dans le projet SUBPERF-AI, qui porte sur une démarche de réduction drastique du cycle de développement de nouveaux concepts sous-marins, en s’appuyant sur les progrès récents de l’intelligence artificielle (IA), et plus particulièrement le machine learning. Au contraire de l’existant en IA basé sur des modèles ininterprétables de type boîte noire, le projet vise à construire une méthodologie de construction de modèles physiques, de complexité adaptée à la physique sous-jacente, en ayant recours à l’expertise humaine et se plaçant comme un outil de conception complémentaire dans l’écosystème existant. Les objectifs principaux du projet sont : Développer une méthodologie de détermination automatisée du modèle d’efforts hydrodynamiques de corps sous-marin, avec utilisation de l’IA (machine learning), sur la base des données de la cinématique, des trajectoires, et des paramètres de contrôle, facilement accessibles, lors des essais maquette ou réel, ou lors d’une simulation numérique. Placer l’expert humain en capacité de contrôler la construction du modèle aux différents stades : qualité des données d’entrée, qualité de la phase d’apprentissage du modèle, et outils/règles de certification a posteriori. La personne recrutée sera intégrée dans une équipe pluridisciplinaire de 3 enseignants-chercheurs, un doctorant et un second post-doctorant. Missions / Activités principales : La personne recrutée prendra en charge la construction d’un modèle d’effort hydrodynamique « expert » et la génération de données expérimentales. Le modèle hydrodynamique expert sera déterminé en suivant la méthodologie classique de l’ITTC, à l’aide d’une campagne d’essais dans la veine aérodynamique pour la caractérisation des efforts (essais en modèle captif du type PMM (Planar Motion Mechanism)). Ce modèle sera implémenté dans un simulateur temporel, dont les résultats seront confrontés sur des manœuvres standards réalisées dans le bassin à drones de l’ENSTA. La confrontation des résultats de trajectoires expérimentales aux trajectoires simulées, obtenues sur la base des essais en modèle captif, pourra amener à questionner la méthodologie standard, en particulier lors de la présence de non-linéarités importantes ou de termes croisés non négligeables. Les essais en bassin fourniront par ailleurs les données de cinématique nécessaires au travail de thèse. Les missions détaillées sont les suivantes : Tâche 1 – conception et fabrication d’un drone sous-marin Conception d’un drone générique de géométrie simplifiée, et instrumenté. Le drone recevra un capotage extérieur, afin de tester plusieurs configurations : géométrie parallélépipédique typique d’un ROV d’exploration, et géométrie cylindrique de type drone torpille. Le drone sera instrumenté pour mesurer les paramètres de contrôle, la cinématique et les trajectoires, ainsi que les efforts propulsifs (poussée, couple) et les efforts de contrôle. Tâche 2 – essais statiques et dynamiques en modèle captif Réalisation d’essais de caractérisation dans la veine aérodynamique de l’ENSTA, en similitude complète de Reynolds, pour les vitesses envisagées d’utilisation en eau du drone. Mesure des efforts en statique, sur les 6 degrés de liberté. Caractérisation des efforts de plans porteurs et du propulseur. Mesure des efforts en dynamique, en mouvement forcé à l’aide de l’hexapode : masses et inerties ajoutées, termes liés aux vitesses angulaires. Tâche 3 – Identification dérivées hydrodynamiques Identification des dérivées hydrodynamiques (ou coefficients hydrodynamiques) à partir des essais en modèle captif. Tâche 4 – Adaptation du simulateur temporel Prise en main du simulateur temporel de l’ENSTA, et de l’environnement de développement. Adaptation du code de calcul pour intégrer des lois de commande issues de mesures expérimentales. Tâche 5 – Essais libres et standardisés, en bassin Réalisation d’essais aux trajectoires prédéfinies (zigzag horizontal ou vertical, accélération horizontale, …). Réalisation d’essais pour parcourir l’espace complet des 6 degrés de libertés. Enregistrement de l’historique des contrôles (vitesse hélice, angles plans porteurs, …), des trajectoires et des efforts des organes de contrôle. Tâche 6 – Rejeu trajectoires simulateur temporel Rejeu numérique des trajectoires, afin de valider si le modèle d’efforts est suffisamment complet pour prédire correctement les trajectoires mesurées expérimentalement. Les résultats obtenus amèneront à publication scientifique. Niveau de diplôme et formations Thèse de doctorat dans le domaine de l’hydrodynamique navale. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. Our mission Build and lead a practical, high-trust health and safety program for Mistral AI’s rapidly expanding data center operations. You will protect employees, contractors and visitors while enabling safe deployment and operation of increasingly dense AI compute infrastructure across colocation sites. You will turn complex operational risks into clear standards, effective controls and measurable improvements. Operating context & accountability You will be the safety partner to Data Center Operations, IT Operations, infrastructure delivery, Security, Legal and People teams, and work directly with colocation operators, installation contractors and OEM service partners. Your remit spans live sites, deployment projects, commissioning and transitions into operations. You will ensure that safety responsibilities are clearly defined and that Mistral-controlled activities meet applicable requirements while challenging partner performance where shared interfaces create risk. Key responsibilities - safety management and compliance Own the operational health and safety management framework for the data center portfolio: policy, critical-risk standards, annual objectives, assurance calendar, risk registers, incident classifications, documentation and management reporting. Interpret applicable occupational health and safety requirements with local specialists; translate them into site-level expectations, control plans and auditable evidence across different countries. Lead regular risk assessments, inspections and assurance reviews; prioritize findings by severity and exposure, assign owners and verify corrective actions have actually reduced risk. Create consistent arrangements for site access, inductions, competency checks, contractor onboarding, safety briefings and refresher training, including evidence of completion. Develop meaningful leading and lagging indicators, including high-potential near misses, overdue critical actions, training coverage, contractor observations and incident trends; present clear recommendations to leadership. Support supplier selection and contract reviews by defining appropriate safety requirements, escalation expectations and minimum standards for colocation and technical service partners. Key responsibilities - operational and technical risk Provide safety oversight for electrical work interfaces, energized equipment, isolation and lockout/tagout, switching coordination, arc-flash exposure and simultaneous activities in live data halls. Assess safe systems of work for heavy rack deliveries, lifting and rigging, material handling, battery systems, working at height, temporary works, confined spaces where relevant and high-density IT installation. Review method statements, risk assessments, permits to work and job safety analyses for high-risk activities, ensuring that scope, boundaries, competence, emergency arrangements and hold points are understood. Partner with engineering teams on the risks introduced by direct-to-chip liquid cooling, CDUs, coolant handling, pressurized circuits, leak detection, hot surfaces and changing rack densities. Participate in readiness reviews before energization, commissioning, major deployments and changes in operating configuration; confirm critical safety issues are resolved or escalated before work proceeds. Coordinate emergency planning and drills with colocation operators and emergency responders for fire, evacuation, electrical incidents, coolant leaks, medical emergencies and loss of critical infrastructure. Key responsibilities - investigations and culture Lead or coordinate investigations of incidents, unsafe conditions and high-potential near misses involving Mistral activities; use structured causal analysis and share actionable learning across the portfolio. Challenge the completeness and quality of provider or contractor investigations when Mistral personnel or equipment may be exposed; track preventive measures through verification. Coach engineers, managers and vendors to identify hazards early, stop unsafe Mistral-controlled work and raise concerns without hesitation. Build strong partnerships with operations, construction, logistics, physical security, compliance and HR; communicate safety expectations clearly in written guidance, training and site discussions. Provide practical support to other regions during major incidents, rapid expansion or unusual operational risk. What success looks like Critical activities are governed by clear, adopted controls and a consistent standard across sites. High-severity findings are visible, owned and resolved; incident learning results in verified preventive action. Site and contractor training, emergency readiness and compliance evidence are maintained and readily accessible. The safety program scales with infrastructure growth without creating unnecessary bureaucracy. Minimum qualifications At least 5 years of practical health and safety experience in operational, industrial, construction or mission-critical environments. Experience implementing safety programs, contractor controls, inspections, risk assessments, investigations and training. Working knowledge of occupational safety regulations and high-risk work controls; ability to coordinate country-specific requirements. Strong communication and influencing skills across technical teams, suppliers and senior stakeholders; fluent professional English. Ability to work regularly on site and travel between data center locations; valid driving licence where required for site access. Preferred qualifications Data center, manufacturing, power infrastructure or complex construction experience involving employees and multiple contractors. Experience with electrical safety, critical mechanical systems, commissioning and work in live operational facilities. Recognized HSE qualification and familiarity with ISO 45001-based management systems. Experience with international portfolios, colocation operators and high-density IT or liquid-cooled systems. arbeitnow-mistral-ai-design-reliability-.title: Design & Reliability Engineering Manager
arbeitnow-mistral-ai-design-reliability-.description: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. Our mission Shape the engineering foundations of Mistral AI’s next generation of compute capacity while improving the resilience of the infrastructure already in service. This role combines technical design leadership with field reliability engineering: you will establish demanding, practical requirements for colocation power and cooling, scrutinize proposed solutions and turn operating experience into better designs, safer changes and more reliable AI capacity. Operating context & accountability Mistral deploys high-density AI infrastructure in colocation facilities, where partners operate the underlying critical plant. You will be Mistral’s technical counterpart to providers, designers, commissioning specialists and internal IT and capacity teams. The position combines forward-looking design authority with hands-on technical investigation and portfolio reliability improvement. It requires depth in one core engineering discipline and the judgment to lead multidisciplinary decisions with specialist support. Key responsibilities — design and technical standards Own and continuously improve Mistral’s technical design criteria and colocation requirements for new facilities, expansions and retrofits, including availability objectives, failure domains, maintainability and operational flexibility. Translate GPU platform roadmaps into measurable facility envelopes: IT load and transients, rack density, electrical topology, redundancy, cooling capacity, supply/return temperatures, flow, pressure, water quality and monitoring. Review utility and MV/LV arrangements, transformers, generators, UPS, switchgear, busway, protection coordination, earthing, power quality and metering for suitability under demanding AI loads. Review mechanical and controls architecture, including chilled-water and heat-rejection systems, pumps, control sequences, CDU integration, leak detection, filtration, water treatment and cooling recovery scenarios. Lead multidisciplinary reviews of single-line diagrams, P&IDs, sequences of operation, design calculations, capacity models, failure-mode studies and proposed deviations; document risks and decisions. Participate in site selection, technical due diligence, provider RFPs, design milestones and commercial technical schedules, challenging assumptions before they become delivery constraints. Define design review and exception processes that balance performance, resilience, deployment speed, efficiency, capital cost and long-term operability. Key responsibilities — commissioning and delivery assurance Partner with delivery and commissioning teams to define functional and integrated testing requirements, acceptance criteria, evidence packages and outstanding-defect management. Validate that electrical and cooling infrastructure can support the contracted AI load envelope under normal, maintenance and credible fault conditions. Review test scripts and results for loss of utility, UPS/generator transitions, cooling component failures, controls faults, CDU interface events and staged restoration where applicable. Ensure operational handover includes accurate drawings, asset and interface registers, monitoring points, setpoints, maintenance constraints, emergency procedures and unresolved risk ownership. Support live-site changes and capacity upgrades with a disciplined review of impact, sequencing, rollback plans and operational readiness. Key responsibilities — field reliability and root-cause analysis Act as a technical escalation point for recurring or high-impact electrical, mechanical and controls incidents across operational colocation sites. Analyze alarms, BMS/EPMS trends, event sequences, power-quality records, cooling telemetry, commissioning findings and maintenance evidence to distinguish symptoms from systemic causes. Lead or challenge technical root-cause investigations with colocation partners, including common-mode failures, protection miscoordination, thermal instability, control logic, hydraulic performance and hidden capacity limitations. Develop risk-ranked corrective actions and reliability improvement programs; validate effectiveness through evidence and post-change monitoring. Identify fleet-wide patterns and feed lessons learned into reference designs, acceptance tests, technical specifications and provider governance. Review maintenance and change proposals that create material exposure to compute availability, providing clear technical recommendations and escalation where required. Key responsibilities — collaboration and leadership Work with IT hardware, network and platform teams to understand the operational consequences of rack-level and cluster-level failure domains. Influence colocation providers, consultants and OEM partners through technically rigorous, fact-based reviews without relying on direct operational authority. Present design trade-offs, reliability risks and investment recommendations in language accessible to engineering leadership and business stakeholders. Develop reusable standards, technical playbooks and engineering knowledge sharing to support consistent decisions across a rapidly expanding portfolio. What success looks like New capacity is accepted against well-defined electrical, thermal and resilience criteria with transparent technical exceptions. Design risks are identified early, reducing late changes, stranded capacity and avoidable operational constraints. Repeat incidents and unresolved critical engineering defects decrease as corrective actions are verified. Field experience produces measurable improvements to future designs and live-site operating resilience. Degree in electrical or mechanical engineering, or equivalent professional experience, with deep knowledge in one discipline and strong working knowledge of the other. Demonstrated expertise in critical power and cooling architecture, redundancy, failure-mode analysis and operational risk management. arbeitnow-mistral-ai-critical-infrastruc.description: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. Our mission Serve as Mistral AI’s senior technical authority for critical electrical, mechanical and life-safety infrastructure across assigned colocation sites. Protect the availability of high-density AI compute by identifying technical risks before they become incidents, challenging infrastructure operating practices and verifying that power and cooling systems perform within agreed requirements. Operating context & accountability Working with Engineering Operations leadership, IT Operations, hardware partners and colocation providers, you will provide hands-on technical assurance across a site or cluster. You will assess provider performance, advise on critical decisions, support incident response and ensure operational learning drives durable improvements. The role focuses on technical oversight and influence rather than direct management of the colocation provider’s maintenance workforce. Technical assurance and operational risk Own and maintain the site technical risk register, including electrical and mechanical single points of failure, maintenance exposure, redundancy limitations, cooling capacity, liquid-cooling interfaces and common-mode failure scenarios. Assess the resilience of utility connections, MV/LV distribution, transformers, generators, UPS, switchgear, busways, protection systems, pumps, cooling plant, controls and monitoring against the contracted operating envelope. Review provider preventive maintenance strategies, schedules, critical asset condition and outstanding defects; identify maintenance deferrals and vulnerabilities that may affect AI compute availability. Critically review high-risk methods of procedure, electrical switching and isolation plans, planned impairments, work sequencing, contingency measures, rollback plans and restoration criteria. Validate the completeness and quality of technical documentation, including single-line diagrams, P&IDs, operating sequences, alarm matrices, capacity records, asset registers and operating procedures. Use BMS/EPMS trends, alarms, power-quality records and cooling telemetry to identify abnormal operating conditions, capacity constraints and deteriorating resilience before service is affected. Incident response, investigations and reliability Act as a senior engineering escalation point during major infrastructure incidents; rapidly assess failure domain, remaining redundancy, safety implications, likely IT impact and viable restoration options. Coordinate technical information across the colocation provider, Mistral IT Operations and OEM partners, ensuring accurate incident timelines, risk communication and controlled return to service. Review and challenge root-cause analyses, distinguishing immediate triggers from underlying design, maintenance, controls, process and organizational contributors. Define and follow up corrective and preventive actions, requesting evidence of implementation and verifying that recurring failure modes have been addressed. Identify systemic trends across sites and share lessons learned with engineering design, commissioning and regional operations teams. Support emergency response planning and tabletop exercises covering loss of utility, cooling failures, liquid leaks, fire/life-safety events and critical equipment failures. Capacity delivery, commissioning and change control Participate in design and constructability reviews for expansions, retrofits and new AI deployments; flag operational, maintainability and resilience concerns early. Review commissioning and integrated systems testing plans, including power transfers, redundancy scenarios, controls failure modes, cooling recovery and operational readiness criteria. Challenge test results and acceptance evidence against defined electrical, thermal and operational requirements; track unresolved technical issues through handover. Partner with IT Operations on rack power and thermal limits, direct-to-chip liquid cooling, coolant distribution unit boundaries, leak response and load-restoration dependencies. Assess proposed changes to critical infrastructure, including concurrent maintenance, controls updates and brownfield works; recommend safeguards and escalation where exposure is unacceptable. Provide technical coaching to internal stakeholders, contribute to engineering standards and support recruitment and knowledge sharing as the portfolio expands. Success measures Critical technical risks are identified early, prioritized and reduced through verified mitigation actions, supporting Mistral’s availability objectives. High-risk maintenance and infrastructure changes receive timely, evidence-based technical review with clear mitigations and escalation. Major incidents are diagnosed accurately, communicated effectively and followed by robust root-cause analysis and verified corrective actions. New and expanded capacity meets agreed redundancy, electrical, cooling and operational acceptance requirements. Repeat failures, unresolved high-severity defects and preventable technical deviations decrease over time. Minimum qualifications 5–7+ years in critical facilities engineering, commissioning, data center operations or technical assurance in high-availability environments. Strong practical knowledge of critical electrical infrastructure (UPS, generators, MV/LV distribution, switchgear and protection) and mechanical systems (cooling plant, pumps, controls and heat rejection). Ability to review single-line diagrams, operating sequences, technical procedures, maintenance plans, commissioning evidence and root-cause analyses. Demonstrated experience troubleshooting complex infrastructure incidents and influencing external technical teams without direct line authority. Clear written and verbal English communication, sound judgment under pressure and willingness to travel and participate in incident escalation as needed. Preferred experience Full technical governance, multi-site operations or mission-critical facilities serving high-density AI/HPC workloads. Experience with direct-to-chip liquid cooling, CDUs, facility/technology cooling interfaces, water quality, leak detection and rack-level thermal management. arbeitnow-mistral-ai-data-center-hardwar.title: Data Center Hardware Engineer
arbeitnow-mistral-ai-data-center-hardwar.description: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. The mission You will work every day on the racks that power one of France's largest AI clusters. Mistral's compute footprint is our single largest investment and the foundation of our AI research and engineering. We're hiring Data Center Hardware Engineers to keep our GPU/CPU clusters healthy, safe and growing — hands-on, in the data center, at the intersection of high-performance computing and physical infrastructure. You'll join a small, senior team working at a scale few engineers get to experience: GPU-dense racks (H100/H200-class and next-generation platforms), high-speed interconnects, liquid-cooled systems — with new sites under development in France and beyond. Hardware here is not someone else's problem. As part of a small on-site team, you carry responsibility for it end to end. Location: On-site at one of our data center in Bessé-sur-Braye, Pays de la Loire. What you'll do Diagnose & repair server and cluster hardware: CPUs, memory, drives, NICs, GPUs, PSUs, and interconnect problems (switches, cables, transceivers; Ethernet/InfiniBand). Intervene safely — power-off/lockout, ESD discipline, pre/post-work checklists, tidy and safe work areas. Capture everything — photos, serials, test results; open, update and close tickets with notes the next engineer can act on. Manage parts — receive, label and track inventory; run RMAs and coordinate with vendors. Help us get better — feed recurring anomalies into monitoring, alerts and SOPs; contribute small scripts (Python/Bash) if you have those skills. Be a good teammate — clear status updates, honest handovers, and respect for the people depending on the cluster. About you Hands-on comfort in data centers or server hardware — you can (or will quickly learn to) work cleanly in racks: rails, cabling, labeling, mounting. Disciplined and meticulous: checklists aren't bureaucracy to you, they're craftsmanship. Practical electrical basics: power-off procedures, PPE, short-circuit risk awareness. Basic Linux (boot checks, logs) — scripting is a plus, not a requirement. Physically able to work in racks (lift, mount, maneuver) in a data center environment. Comfortable in a 24/7 operation, including a rotating on-call with emergency response expectations. Driver's licence (B) for travel between our sites. Even if you don't match every criterion Many of our best hardware engineers came from research labs, telecoms, IT services or the military. If you are rigorous, curious and genuinely motivated by hardware at scale, we would be glad to hear from you — we assess demonstrated scope rather than keyword matching. Nice to have HPC/AI/cloud production experience at scale; large-fleet server install and maintenance. Networking fundamentals (Ethernet/InfiniBand) beyond basics. Vendor/RMA tooling, ticketing (Jira/ServiceNow), inventory systems. Python/Bash automation for checks, capture, inventory or reporting. What We Offer We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page . Privacy Policy Your privacy matters to us. arbeitnow-alta-ares-bid-project-manager-.title: Bid & Project Manager – EU & NATO (H/F)
arbeitnow-alta-ares-bid-project-manager-.description: About Alta Ares Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them. Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia. Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development. Role & Mission NATO agencies & EU programs are investing in counter-drone capability now, and Alta Ares answers a fast-growing flow of their tenders and calls for proposals. As Bid & Project Manager in our EU, NATO & Eastern Flank team, you turn each opportunity into a compliant offer, then into a project delivered on time. Your sales director owns the customer relationship and the commercial strategy; you own the offer and its delivery. This is not a one-programme job. You will run several bids and projects at once: a NATO bid, an EU grant proposal, and an RFI can land in the same week, and none of them can slip. This is a demanding, high-ownership role. Deadlines do not move, the stakes are real, and the team will rely on you to hold the line. We are looking for someone who wants that responsibility. Bid Management - from first read to submission Screen and qualify opportunities with your sales director; prepare bid/no-bid decisions with risks, resources, and price on the table Break each tender down (NATO IFB or RFQ, EU call, RFP for a Nation through EU-NATO platforms such as NSPA or SAFE joint procurement) into a compliance matrix, a bid plan and clear owners Write and assemble the management, technical and compliance volumes with Engineering, Product, Finance and Legal Organise the review gates and prepare the final price review with Finance; submit complete, compliant and on time, every time Run the clarification rounds and support your sales director in negotiations through to contract signature NATO & EU Procurement - the rules of the game Master NSPA and NCIA procedures: Source File registration, declarations of eligibility, notifications of intent, IFBs and RFQs, basic ordering agreements and framework contracts Run EU grant proposals (European Defence Fund, EDIP): Funding & Tenders portal, consortium building, Part A and Part B, lump-sum budgets Track national procurement rules and partners on the Eastern Flank through EU-NATO (Poland, Romania, the Baltic States…), e.g. via NSPA or SAFE joint procurement Build and maintain the bid library: company documents, CVs, past performance, standard answers, templates Project Delivery - from award to acceptance Turn each award into a project: kick-off, plan, milestones, risks, budget and change control Coordinate engineering, production, demo and logistics teams, and partners, to deliver what we promised when we promised it Own customer reporting, deliverables and acceptance (FAT/SAT), with the documentation trail for invoicing and audits Run several projects in parallel, each at a different stage Process & Reporting Set the bid and project rhythm for the team: calendar, gates, templates, dashboards Review the status of every live bid and project weekly with your sales director: deadlines, compliance, risks, resources needed Run lessons learned after every bid, won or lost Candidate Profile 5+ years in bid, proposal or project management in defence, aerospace or security Proven record of compliant, on-time submissions to NATO agencies, EU programmes or European ministries of defence, several of them in parallel At least one defence contract delivered from award to acceptance Scale-up or lean-team experience is a significant advantage; prime experience is welcome if you want more breadth and speed Skills & Qualities Rigorous and precise compliance is binary; in defence, the margin for error is zero Built for parallel work you run several bids and projects at once, prioritise hard and never drop the ball Committed you own the outcome, not just your part of it; submission peaks are part of the job and you plan for them Calm under pressure fixed deadlines, late amendments and competing requests do not throw you A clear writer structured, scoreable English; you turn engineering input into compliant answers A leader without authority you get engineers, Finance, Legal and partners to deliver on time Technically curious you understand how sensors, effectors, C2 and AI fit together, or you learn it fast Discreet and trustworthy you handle sensitive commercial and defence information as a matter of course Mission-driven you care about European security, not just the job title Nice to Have APMP, Shipley, PMP, PRINCE2 or IPMA certification Experience on a European Defence Fund or EDIP consortium, or with NSPA/NCIA procurement A background in a NATO agency, the EDA or a ministry of defence, or military service (officer or NCO) Knowledge of C-UAS, air defence, ISR or drones Export-control experience (French export licensing, EU dual-use rules) Security This position will require applying for a NATO personnel security clearance; it is therefore open to nationals of EU Member States that are also NATO members, and the hire is subject to the clearance procedure Languages Professional English, written and spoken (C1) is mandatory French is a strong plus Polish, Romanian, Lithuanian or Ukrainian is a plus Travel Regular travel to NATO agencies (Brussels, Luxembourg, The Hague), EU institutions, and to demos and acceptance tests across Europe Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

We're a global marketplace for refurbished devices, helping lower our collective environmental impact by providing trustworthy, affordable tech with 92% less carbon emissions than new. Yep, you read that right. Turns out refurbished tech is way better for the planet than new. In fact, With every device purchased on Back Market, our positive impact on the planet grows. From our Customer Care representatives to our software engineer, every individual at Back Market cuts the planet — and consumers — a break. Our mission is simple: to do more with what we already have. Are you ready to join us? The Sellers Operations & Intelligence team being the backbone of the Seller Success Department, drives convergence, efficiency, and data-driven insights across all seller channels and geographies. Key Responsibilities Improve the tools, dashboards, and reporting used by Seller Success Managers to monitor seller performance Support team routines and workflows by simplifying processes and reducing manual work Run and optimize seller programs operations, especially our seller incentive programs Ensure data quality and reporting accuracy for business reviews and decision-making Partner with Seller Success Manager, Analytics, and Product teams to implement scalable solutions Identify opportunities to use AI and automation to improve efficiency and insight generation.
